From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: 429/5xx spike — production requests failing, urgent

On it. Quick findings from initial triage:
- PagerDuty incident INC123456 opened at 08:06 ET, Datadog shows a sharp 429 spike coincident with FintechCo's traffic pattern.
- A subset of requests are getting 429 with X-RateLimit-Reset far in the future (~3600s). Many clients are retrying aggressively (no Retry-After honor) causing retry storm.
- Seeing a misapplied org-level quota: FintechCo has an org cap configured in our routing layer that is lower than the project-level reserved tier they purchased. Traffic routing/ tiering logic double-enforced the cap for a subset of routes (product bug we rolled last week).
- Some 5xx (502/504) appear downstream (inference runtime node timeouts) when burst traffic exhausts concurrency pools.

Mitigation enacted (08:24 ET):
1) Temporarily raised the org cap for FintechCo to match their committed tier (manual override).
2) Applied conservative circuit breaker (reject fast) on routing path to prevent cascading backend timeouts.
3) Added Retry-After header suggestions on 429 responses.

Status: partial reduction in 429s after manual override; monitoring to watch for residual retry storms.

I’ll keep this open and follow up with a root cause write-up.

Marcus Lin
SRE — Inference Platform
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 11:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: 429/5xx spike — production requests failing, urgent

Looping in Evelyn per Marissa's ask for executive visibility. Short technical summary and next steps for a durable fix:
- Root cause hypothesis: a recent change to routing policy (tiered quotas) had an edge-case where org-level caps were applied twice when route metadata matched both org and project tags. This causes earlier-than-expected 429s for mid-to-high concurrency clients.
- Action items:
  * Immediate (today): add a validation gate in the routing control plane to detect mismatched caps and fail open rather than double-enforce (rollback if required). Target: 4 hours.
  * Short-term (72 hours): release a patch to ensure single-source quota resolution and more conservative defaults for Retry-After / backoff headers.
  * Medium-term (2 weeks): add an automated drift detector alert that flags when org cap != sum(project caps) and tie to playbook.
- Communications: prepare customer note templates and a recommended backoff snippet we can share with FintechCo.

Requesting Evelyn's signoff to treat this as an executive incident (notify CRO/VP Sales) due to revenue impact and possibility of renewals friction.

—Hiro
Director, Serving Runtime Engineering
hiro.tanaka@redwood.com
